newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up 2.19 pct on bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up 2.19 pct on bargain hunting.

text.p: Battered Thai stocks, which fell in four successive sessions this week, rose 2.19 percent on Friday as bargain hunters bought cheap finance and bank issues for speculative reasons, brokers said.

"Bargain hunters bought finance and banking stocks today as they believed that stocks on both counters had been oversold earlier this week. Foreigners bought a lot of Siam Commercial Bank stocks today," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico Securities.
The SET index finished 14.80 points higher at 691.45 on 5.6 billion baht turnover.
The SET-50 index advanced 1.44 points to 50.82.
Gainers led decliners 254 to 102 while 59 issues ended unchanged.
Brokers said there was nothing changed in the market's fundamentals and investors were still concerned about the health of finance firms after new measures were imposed by the central bank on Monday.

Under the Bank of Thailand's order, commercial banks and finance firms are required to raise provisions for poor quality assets. Ten finance firms, hit by liquidity crunches, are also required to raise their capital.
Dhana Siam Finance topped the active list, rising 3.50 baht to 39.75. Siam Commercial Bank advanced two to 130 and PTT Exploration and Production surged 22 to 330.
"I believe that the buying today was meant for short-term investment because most investors are still worried about the liquidity of finance companies," one broker said.

Some analysts said the market gained after plunging to more than a 4-1/2 year low on Thursday on some investor confidence that measures imposed by the authorities could strengthen the financial sector in the long term.
The finance sector gained the most, rising 6.02 percent. The communication sector rose 3.23 percent while the banking sector advanced 1.67 percent and the property sector declined 0.64 percent.
